'''Frances Colón''' is an American [[Science diplomacy|science diplomat]] and [[environmental policy]] expert most notably having served at the [[United States Department of State]] between September 2008 and January 2017. In her work, she promotes the integration of science and technology into foreign policy dialogues; global scientific engagement for capacity-building; the advancement of women in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]]; and the use of innovation as a tool for economic growth around the world.<ref name=":0" />

Previously, Dr. Colón served the U.S. Department of State as the Science and Environment Adviser at the Western Hemisphere Affairs Bureau where she was responsible for advising on environmental and scientific issues that affected the [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. Government]]'s [[foreign policy]] objectives in the Americas. During that time, Dr. Colón coordinated [[Politics of climate change|climate change policy]] for the [[Energy and Climate Partnership of the Americas]] announced by [[Barack Obama|President Barack Obama]] in 2009. As a [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|AAAS]] Science and Technology Policy Fellow (2006–2008), Dr. Colón led the OES Bureau’s program for Muslim world outreach through [[K–12|K-12]] science and math education cooperation.<ref name=":0" />

In November 2020, Colón was named a volunteer member of the [[Presidential transition of Joe Biden|Joe Biden presidential transition]] Agency Review Team to support transition efforts related to the [[United States Department of State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Agency Review Teams |url=https://buildbackbetter.com/the-transition/agency-review-teams/ |website=President-Elect Joe Biden |access-date=10 November 2020 |archive-date=28 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828180800/https://www.whitehouse.gov/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Since 2021, she has been a member of the [[President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology]] (PCAST).<ref>{{cite web|title=President Biden Announces Members of President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology |url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2021/09/22/president-biden-announces-members-of-presidents-council-of-advisors-on-science-and-technology/|website=[[White House]]|date=22 September 2021 |access-date=2022-08-27}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Dr. Colón grew up in [[San Juan, Puerto Rico]] and earned her B.S. in biology in 1997 from the [[University of Puerto Rico]]. She went on to earn her doctorate in [[Developmental Neurobiology|developmental neurobiology]] at [[Brandeis University]] in 2004.<ref name="Frances Colón">{{Cite web|title=Leadership in Government Fellowship|url=https://www.opensocietyfoundations.org/grants/leadership-in-government-fellowship?fellow=frances-colon&current=1|access-date=2020-07-12|website=Open Society Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== Science diplomacy career ===
She served nearly five years as deputy science and technology adviser to the [[Secretary of state|Secretary of State]] (2012–2017).<ref>{{Cite news|last=Johnson|first=Whitney|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/whitneyjohnson/2017/08/09/when-its-time-to-reinvent-reach-back-to-your-roots/#250645991f8b|title=When It's Time To Reinvent, Reach Back To Your Roots|date=2017-08-09|work=Forbes|access-date=2018-06-02|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://2009-2017.state.gov/e/stas/staff/index.htm|title=Staff and Contact Information|website=2009-2017.state.gov|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref> In that role, she became the highest-ranking [[Hispanic]] scientist at the State Department. Prior to this role, she had been an adviser on science and the environment for the Western Hemisphere Affairs at the State Department<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://fortyover40.com/2016-honorees/frances-colon/|title=Frances Colón|website=fortyover40.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref> and served as acting science and technology adviser to Secretary of State [[John Kerry]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Richard Stone|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/state-department-science-adviser-speaks-out-cuba|title=State Department science adviser speaks out on Cuba|date=2015-05-14|work=Science {{!}} AAAS|access-date=2018-06-02|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2015, she represented the United States government as vice chair of the [[United Nations]] Commission on Science and Technology Development.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://geneva.usmission.gov/2015/05/04/statement-by-dr-frances-colon-at-the-un-commission-on-science-and-technology-for-development/|title=Statement by Dr. Frances Colon at the UN Commission on Science and Technology for Development » US Mission Geneva|website=geneva.usmission.gov|date=4 May 2015|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Under Secretary of State [[Hillary Clinton]], Colón led the [[Energy and Climate Partnership of the Americas|Energy and Climate Partnership for the Americas]] (ECPA), an initiative announced by President Obama at the [[Summits of the Americas|Summit of the Americas]] in April 2009 to accelerate [[sustainable energy]] in the Americas.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ecpamericas.org/|title=ECPA Homepage|website=ecpamericas.org|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://2009-2017.state.gov/p/wha/rls/fs/240498.htm|title=Energy and Climate Partnership of the Americas|work=U.S. Department of State|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.doi.gov/oia/press/2010/The-US-Virgin-Islands-and-Puerto-Rico-Meet-to-Explore-Collaboration-in-Utilities|title=The U.S. Virgin Islands and Puerto Rico Meet to Explore Collaboration in Utilities|website=doi.gov|date=17 June 2015|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref>

=== Science advocacy efforts ===
Colón is also an outspoken advocate for women and girls to pursue careers in science.<ref name=":1" /> During her time as Deputy Adviser, she oversaw the creation of the [https://2009-2017.state.gov/e/stas/c57937.htm Networks of Diasporas in Engineering and Science] (NODES) initiative to empower diasporas with science expertise to develop and influence effective policies and solve challenges in their countries of origin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://2009-2017.state.gov/e/stas/c57937.htm|title=Networks of Diasporas in Engineering and Science (NODES) Homepage|website=2009-2017.state.gov|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref><ref name="Frances Colón" /> As part of [[Barack Obama|President Obama's]] White House "Untold History of Women in STEM" project, she shared the story of [[Puerto Ricans|Puerto Rican]] scientist [[Ana Roque de Duprey|Ana Roqué de Duprey]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/node/311241|title=The Untold History of Women in Science and Technology|website=The White House|language=en|access-date=2020-04-09}}</ref>
